title: Gaia-based stellar data reduce the duration excess of KOI-3105.01 in a Kepler DR25 test
abstract: We tested long transit durations in the Kepler DR25 catalog. A screen of 346 high-score candidates selected KOI-3105.01. Its reported duration is 3.36 times the maximum central circular duration under the DR25 stellar model. The Gaia-based mass and radius from Berger et al. (2020) reduce this ratio to 1.16. Favorable changes within the quoted input errors can bridge the remaining excess. Thus, the old duration excess does not establish high eccentricity. A fixed-time check of four Kepler quarters gives a pooled dip in both SAP and PDC flux. The later quarters are weak. These data do not locate the host or independently measure the duration. The stellar-model errors lack a joint covariance, and a blended source or detector effect is not excluded. We find no new planet. The package contains the catalog screen, source records, four light curves, hashes, code, uncertainty checks, a figure, and offline reproduction instructions.

display.caption: The revised stellar model reduces the mean duration excess. Four Kepler quarters show a weak pooled dip. The model error bar is a mass-radius sensitivity box, not a confidence interval.
